pl-l3d22c2-d1e115.summary: Asks whether Christ in death was a man anywhere, and whether he is a man wherever he is.

pl-l3d22c2-d1e118.summary: Answers that he was not, and is not now, man wherever he is: he is everywhere according to deity, but not everywhere united to a man; where he is according to the man, there he is man. In death he was everywhere as God, in hell according to the soul and in the tomb according to the flesh, man in both, though not united to the whole humanity in either.
claims: Christ is not man everywhere he is.
In death Christ was in hell by the soul and in the tomb by the flesh, and man in both places.

pl-l3d22c2-d1e121.summary: Objects: if in hell he was united only to the soul and in the tomb only to the flesh, then in neither place was he united to soul and flesh; how is he called man there?

pl-l3d22c2-d1e125.summary: Replies that by one and the same union he was united to the soul in hell and to the flesh in the tomb, and so to both, though separated, as before death.
claims: Christ was united to soul and flesh by one and the same union, even when they were separated.

pl-l3d22c2-d1e128.summary: Raises a further objection: had Christ assumed only soul or only flesh, he would not have been a true man; so where he did not have both united, he was not a true man. But in death he had them united nowhere, so he was nowhere a man.

pl-l3d22c2-d1e131.summary: Replies that Christ would not have been a true man without assuming both soul and flesh; but having assumed them he put down neither and kept unceasingly the same union contracted in assuming. So wherever he is united to soul, flesh, or both, he is fittingly called man, being 'humanated' there. He was man in the tomb and in hell at once, lying in the tomb by the flesh alone and descending to hell by the soul alone.
claims: Christ never put down soul or flesh after assuming them.
Christ is called man wherever he is united to soul, flesh, or both.
Christ lay in the tomb by the flesh and descended to hell by the soul at the same time.

pl-l3d22c2-d1e134.summary: Quotes Augustine: who was not left in hell? Christ, but in the soul only; who lay in the tomb? Christ, but in the flesh only; since Christ is in each, we confess Christ in all and each.
claims: Christ is confessed to be in hell by the soul and in the tomb by the flesh.

pl-l3d22c2-d1e143.summary: Draws out that Christ was united to the flesh lying in the tomb as to the soul in hell; otherwise he could not be said to have lain there. The soul descended to hell, the flesh lay in the tomb, and Wisdom remained with both, as Ambrose says, shedding the light of eternal life in hell without being enclosed by it, since Wisdom is in no time or place and death cannot be ascribed to it; on the cross the flesh hung, not the divine substance.
claims: Christ's flesh in the tomb remained united to him.
Wisdom remained with soul and flesh and illumined hell without being confined.
Death is not ascribed to the divine Wisdom.

pl-l3d22c2-d1e161.summary: Concludes: we confess that Christ hung on the cross and lay in the tomb in the flesh, and was in hell in the soul alone.
claims: Christ hung and lay in the flesh, and was in hell in the soul alone.

pl-l3d22c2.summary: Asks whether Christ in death was a man anywhere, and whether he is a man wherever he is. He is not a man wherever he is, since he is everywhere by deity but not everywhere united to humanity; but wherever he is according to the man, there he is man. In death he was in the tomb according to the flesh and in hell according to the soul, and was man in both places, though not united to the whole humanity in either. Against the objection that he was nowhere united to both together and so nowhere man, Lombard answers that he never put down either, but kept one and the same union with both, though separated, so he is fittingly called man wherever he was 'humanated'. Augustine and Ambrose confirm: Christ lay in the tomb in the flesh only and was in hell in the soul only, while Wisdom remained with both and lit up hell without being confined by it.
claims: Christ is not a man wherever he is, but is man wherever he is according to the humanity.
In death Christ was in the tomb by the flesh and in hell by the soul.
Christ kept one and the same union with soul and flesh when they were separated.
Christ was man in the tomb and in hell because he was 'humanated' there.
